title: Throughput oddball signal dig — warmup hysteresis + KV cache interplay
content:
Context:
Summary of the sync on an odd, intermittent throughput/latency signal we observed across several shadow runs on 80G A100 pools. Signal appears during staggered warmup scenarios (mixed sequence lengths) and manifests as periodic p95 spikes and ~2.5–3.5x drops in sustained QPS for short 30–90s windows. Not reproducible on every run; correlates with cache refill patterns and recent attention-kernel rollout.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Liam O'Rourke
- Sofia Alvarez
- Ravi Desai
- Evan Park
- Tara Nguyen (observability)

Meeting notes / raw observations:
- First noticed in shadow-run on 2026-09-08 during mixed-seq sweep. Baseline run (no kernel changes) steady at ~1.6k QPS, p50 11–14ms, p95 42–55ms. After kernel roll (attention-v2) p95 intermittent jumps to 150–190ms during short windows, and sustained QPS drops to ~500–700 for ~30–90s.
- Not all machines show the spike. Affected hosts share: older driver (CUDA 535.86), colocated debug sidecar, and host-level cron that killed an LTO prefetch process at 03:20 UTC.
- Spike strongly correlates with sequences >1024 tokens being introduced in a short burst (50–100 concurrent seqs). Hypothesis: KV cache refill + attention kernel path switch causes memory traffic spikes and scheduler backpressure.
- Observability notes: heatmap shows CPU steal and NVLink burst on node n10-az2 during events; GPU SM utilization dips while latency rises — suggests GPU stalls waiting on memory transfers.

Test matrix run during sync (commands, configs):
- Run harness: infra/perf/harness/staggered_mixed_seq.py --model redwood-4x --gpu-pool 80G-A100 --instances 16 --seq-distribution "mix:60%<256,30%512-1024,10%>1024" --duration 10m
- Baseline (pre-rollout): 2026-09-05 02:10 UTC
  - sustained QPS: 1,620
  - p50 latency: 12ms
  - p95 latency: 47ms
  - max mem bw (nvlink): 880 GB/s
- Post-rollout (attention-v2): 2026-09-08 03:00 UTC (spike observed)
  - typical sustained QPS: 1,550
  - spike window(s): QPS drop to 520 / p95 172ms (avg 3 windows per 10m run)
  - nvlink bursts aligned with p95 windows, CPU steal + io wait increased by ~17%
- Isolation run (single tenant, cold-start disabled): 2026-09-10 08:20 UTC
  - sustained QPS: 1,560
  - single spike observed (one 45s window): QPS 610, p95 160ms
- Experiment: force small-batch-path (max_batch=4)
  - sustained QPS dropped (expected) to 1,020 but spikes disappeared in 3/3 runs
- Experiment: disable KV cache prefetch (kv_prefetch=false)
  - spikes reduced (1/5 runs) but overall p50/p95 slightly worse; indicates KV prefetch timing relevant

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- "[2026-09-08T03:21:12Z] pool-n10-az2: nvlink: burst 1.1TB/s, kernel-switch attention-v2, kv-refill start, inflight-batches=46"
- "[2026-09-08T03:21:58Z] pool-n10-az2: scheduler: backpressure on queue 3, active-lanes reduced"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Attention-v2 path introduces contention on device-side staging buffers during KV refill bursts for long sequences. Some kernels perform fallback transfers that block SM progress until DMA completes.
2) Warmup hysteresis: our autoscaler/warmer allows many inflight long-seq requests before KV cache temperature stabilizes, causing periodic cache reheating and memory-bandwidth saturation.
3) Host-level interference (cron/sidecars) amplifies the memory stall windows — correlated but not sufficient to explain all events.
4) Scheduler batching heuristics can produce pathological windows when mixed-seq distribution has short bursts of long sequences; batching max size + lane assignment can starve short-request lanes.

Immediate mitigation ideas tried (and results):
- Lower max_batch to 4: removed spikes but reduced QPS by ~35% — acceptable as a stopgap for critical tenants.
- Disable KV prefetch: reduced frequency of spikes but increased average token latency.
- Pin long-seq requests to dedicated lanes (experimental): promising in lab; needs routing policy update.

Proposed experiments (next 72 hours):
1) Reproduce with forced DMA logging on affected nodes (owner: Ravi, due: 2026-09-13). Capture time-aligned nvlink and pci-e stats.
2) Run attention-v2 with smaller staging buffer (config param staging_buf_target_mb) across 6 hosts to measure sensitivity (owner: Liam, due: 2026-09-14).
3) Introduce transient lane isolation in shadow-running traffic to validate if lane allocation solves bursts (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-09-14).
4) Create short-lived routing rule to route sequences >1024 to a ‘longseq’ lane with lower concurrency and prewarmed KV (owner: Maya, due: 2026-09-15).
5) Add a benchmark that replays realistic startup traffic (scheduled cron) to catch hysteresis earlier (owner: Tara, due: 2026-09-13).

Longer-term items:
- Kernel rollback plan (if experiment 2 shows regressions) and mitigations funnel into INF-3124.
- Investigate scheduler heuristics that can dynamically detect and throttle long-seq bursts without lowering overall throughput.
- Update canary/shadow criteria to include mixed-seq warmup scenarios in weekly smoke tests.

Action items (owners & blockers):
- Ravi: enable DMA nvlink trace capture on n10-az2 and n11-az1; needs node-level access escalation (blocked by infra ticket INF-3201).
- Liam: run attention-v2 staging_buf sensitivity sweep, collect perf counters and kernel timing. (needs CI slot 4 reserved).
- Sofia: implement temporary lane-tag routing in shadow infra; no customer impact.
- Tara: add warmup-mixed-seq test to perf-cron and increase retention of per-run traces from 3d to 14d for analysis.
- Maya: coordinate rollback plan if mitigations fail; prepare customer-facing note if SLA impact observed.

Open questions / risks:
- Is the observed NVLink burst magnitude expected for the model+batching profile? (ask kernel team)
- Does attention-v2 intentionally change staging behavior for >1024 sequences? (ask model-intel)
- Can we cheaply detect imminent spike windows and temporarily throttle long-seq acceptance?

Decisions made in-sync:
- Do not rollback globally yet; we will run the isolation and sensitivity experiments and decide by 2026-09-15.
- Apply lane-routing in shadow for 48h beginning 2026-09-13.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Collect full perf counters (pcie_read/write, nvlink util, SM stall reasons) for 3 spike windows and attach to INF-3124.
- Add a short script to tag runs where p95 > 3x baseline and auto attach traces to ticket.

References / related tickets and PRs:
- INF-3124 (regression tracking)
- PR: serving-runtime#678 (attention-v2 rollout notes + perf notes)
- Infra: INF-3201 (node access escalation)
- Slack thread: #perf (link above)

Appendix — brief reproduction checklist:
1) Checkout serving-runtime@pr/678
2) Start harness with --seq-distribution mix:60%<256,30%512-1024,10%>1024 --duration 10m --enable-shadow-routing false
3) Collect nvlink+pci counters (nvlinkmon) and kernel timing (nvprof-like)
4) Run three repeats and tag runs where p95 > 120ms

If you want more raw logs from today's isolation runs, ping me in Slack and I'll drop the archive (50MB) to the INF-3124 ticket.

-- Maya
